A B S T R A C T
In this paper, five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts, including a new highly efficient through-hole
(TH) electroplating leveler, were synthesized from environmentally harmless coumarin compounds. The inhib
itory properties of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts were tested by electrochemical method,
leading to the selection of the optimal leveler (C2). The adsorption capacity, adsorption state and adsorption sites
of different coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts on copper surface were systematically analyzed, and the
reasons for the different inhibition capacity of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts with different
molecular structures were explained. The effect of C2 content on throwing power (TP) was studied, when C2
content was only 0.6 ppm, TP value was greater than 100 %. The adsorption behavior of C2 on copper cathode
and the interaction between C2 and other additives were studied by the galvanostatic measurements (GMs). SEM
and XRD tests were conducted to analyze the effects of different amounts of C2 on the copper plating surface.

4-bipyridine can be used to connect

ammonium salts. If such large flat molecules can be adsorbed on copper
surfaces, they have the potential to be effective levelers [15,34]. As a

crystal surface of copper particles. GMs results show that C2 can exert

behavior. C2 has competitive adsorption with SPS, no interaction with
Cl<sup>-</sup>, and synergistic inhibition with PEG to form stable PEG-C2 com-
plexes. This study expanded the application of coumarin derivatives and
the design range of electroplating leveler molecules, hoping to provide
some reference ideas for the development of more efficient levele
molecules in the future.

2. Material and methods
2.1. Synthesis and structural characterization
The reagents used in this study are commercially available. Unless
otherwise stated, they were used directly without further purification. In
this work, five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts A1 − C2
(Fig. 2) were synthesized. The synthesis route and characterization are
shown in the supporting information.
2.2. Electrochemical test
The electrochemical analysis in this study was carried out in a three-
electrode system using an electrochemical workstation (PGSTAT302N,
Auto-Lab). All the electrochemical test conditions were consistent, and
the concentration of e32 in the Virgin Make-up Solution (VMS) was 3.68

2.3. Quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulation
Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dy-
namics (MD) simulations were implemented to calculate the adsorption
capacity and the adsorption state of compounds A1 − C2 on copper from
a theoretical level. Quantum chemistry calculations were based on DFT,
the B3LYP function and def2-SVP basis set. The Gaussian 09 program
was used to optimize the species geometry. Vibrational frequencies were
calculated to evaluate the nature of the optimized structures at the same
level. Next, the contour surfaces of the highest occupied molecular or
bitals (HOMOs) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMOs)
were visualized with Avogadro program. Electrostatic potential (ESP)
surfaces were generated by Multiwfn and VMD software.

2.4. TH electroplating and copper electroplating surface micro
morphology
In this study, a 1.5 L Haring tank was used for TH electroplating
experiments. The anode was a phosphorous copper plate, and a printed
circuit board (PCB) with a certain number of THs was used as the
cathode for electrodeposition. Sections of the PCB board after electro
deposition were made into a metallographic section, and the throwing
power (TP) of the copper boards was observed using a metallographic
microscope (zeiss, Axio Observer A1m). The calculation method of TP
value is shown in Equation (1) and Fig. 3[26,34,35].
The micro morphology of the copper-plated surface was observed by
scanning electron microscope (SEM, Hitachi S-3400 N), the crystal plane
orientation of the copper-plated layers was analyzed by X-ray diffrac-
tometer (XRD, Rigaku, 18KW/D/max 2550VB/PC). The diffraction
patterns were recorded in the 2θ range of 30◦~80◦, the change of each
step was 0.02◦, and the scanning speed was 6◦/min.

4. Conclusion
In summary, this study synthesized five coumarin-based quaternary
ammonium salts and, for the first time, investigated their application as
novel electroplating levelers in acid copper plating. Electrochemical
measurements were used to analyze the copper plating inhibition ability
of five coumarin-based quaternary ammonium salts, leveler C2 with
double coumarin structure had the strongest inhibition performance.
Quantum chemical calculation and MD simulation show that leveler C2
has the strongest adsorption capacity and the most adsorption sites on
copper surface, which is the reason why C2 has the strongest inhibition
ability. TH copper plating results show that the leveler C2 has good
leveling performance, only need 0.6 ppm addition, can get 103.36 %
through-hole TP value. The interaction between C2 and other additives
and the mechanism of action were further explored by GMs test. The
results of SEM and XRD show that the leveler C2 can make the surface of
the copper plating layer smoother and optimize the orientation of the
copper crystallographic plane. In this work, a new coumarin compound
was synthesized for the first time and used as an electroplating leveler,
which expanded the application range of coumarin compounds and the
design field of molecular structure of electroplating leveler. It is hoped
that it can be used as the basis for the development of efficient leveler
molecules in the future.
